Person.name: Elena Marchetti
Person.summary: Elena Marchetti is a physicist known for her work on low-temperature superconductivity; her 1987 paper reshaped the field's understanding of critical currents. She taught at the University of Turin for three decades and received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1991.

LifeExperience.title: Born in Turin, Italy
LifeExperience.description: Elena Marchetti was born to a family of clockmakers in Turin.

LifeExperience.title: Doctorate in Physics
LifeExperience.description: Completed her doctorate at the University of Turin, studying magnetic properties of metals at low temperature.

LifeExperience.title: Joined the University of Turin faculty
LifeExperience.description: Began teaching solid-state physics; established the Low Temperature Laboratory in 1965.

LifeExperience.title: Retired from teaching
LifeExperience.description: Retired after 33 years, continuing research as professor emerita.

Achievement.title: Best Paper Award, European Physical Society
Achievement.description: Recognised for the 1987 paper on critical currents in superconducting alloys.

Achievement.title: Nobel Prize in Physics
Achievement.description: Awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for her discoveries concerning low-temperature superconductivity.

Achievement.title: Honorary Doctorate, ETH Zurich
Achievement.description: Conferred in recognition of three decades of research and teaching.

Achievement.title: "Currents at the Edge" published
Achievement.description: Her most cited paper, on critical currents in superconducting alloys.
